decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: 'I chose these fields... Title and Description being the ones auto-filled'. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon AND preview image; only title+description were auto-collected. Round 3 client: 'I'd also like it to collect the site icon and a preview image automatically when available; I wouldn't need to edit those manually.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Divergence established independently: presented auto-fill omits favicon+preview image required by REF-BM-02. Client requests the missing related reference behavior -> corrective/extend. Implemented in round 4.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: 'Tags are entered as plain text separated by commas... Tell me if you'd expect to enter or pick tags a different way.' No autocomplete of existing tags (REF-BM-10). Round 5 client: 'once I have existing tags, I'd like suggestions to appear as I type so I can reuse them consistently.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented tag entry lacks REF-BM-10 autocomplete of existing tags. Client extends to request it. The round-6 A/B (dropdown vs inline Tab) is a functionally-equivalent UI selection both fulfilling REF-BM-10, so excluded; this decision is the requirement expression, counted once.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: 'Newly saved links appear at the top of the list (most recent first). Let me know if that's the order you'd want.' No sort control existed. Round 5 client: 'Most-recent-first is a good default, though I'd eventually like to change the sorting.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Divergence: prototype had a fixed order with no sort-key selection required by REF-BM-22. Client extends to request changeable sorting. Implemented in round 10 (four sort choices), which conforms; not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: 'Search looks across the title, site, tags, and your notes... Tell me if that's the right breadth.' REF-BM-12 requires title, description, note AND url. Presented scope omits description and url. Round 7 client: 'please include the full web address and the description too, so I can find a bookmark from any part I remember.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Divergence established from the enumerated search scope missing url+description. Client extends breadth to reference set. Split from case-insensitivity (separable REF item). Implemented round 8.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presentation of search did not address case handling. Round 7 client: 'Search should ignore capitalization as well.' Round 8 maker confirms it now 'ignores capitalization throughout' (added alongside url/description), indicating it was case-sensitive before.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-sensitive search contradicts REF-BM-13; client supplies the conforming case-insensitive behavior. Divergence corroborated by round-8 'now ignores capitalization' being grouped with the newly-added items.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: 'picking a tag filters to that one tag (not adding several tags together). Tell me if one-at-a-time is fine or if you'd expect to stack multiple tags.' Round 9 client: 'Filtering by one tag at a time is sufficient for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Single-tag filtering conforms to REF-BM-11 ('filter to only that tag's bookmarks'); multi-tag stacking is beyond the reference. The A/B (filter bar vs click-tag-on-card) is a functionally-equivalent UI selection, excluded. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker: 'read later as a marker you put on a bookmark that's already saved... Read later is just a focused view... Taking it off the read-later list does not delete the bookmark.' Round 11 client: 'Yes, this matches how I think about it... marking something as read should remove it from that view without deleting the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented behavior conforms to REF-BM-17 (mark read-later), REF-BM-18 (separate view), REF-BM-19 (mark read removes from list). No departure from reference despite the maker offering a separate-place alternative; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: 'Archiving hides a bookmark from All bookmarks (and Read later), but never deletes it... restorable... Archived items don't appear in normal searching/sorting.' Round 12 client: 'archiving behaves the way I want. It removes the bookmark... without deleting it, keeps it in a separate Archived tab, and lets me restore it. Hiding archived items from normal search is also right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforms to REF-BM-26 (hide from default list/search, keep content), REF-BM-27 (reversible vs delete), REF-BM-28 (separate archived list). Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker: 'On a duplicate, I warn but don't block — you decide whether to keep two copies... with Save anyway or Cancel... should it hard-block duplicates?' Round 13 client: 'For duplicates, I don't want Save anyway. Please prevent a second copy and take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it instead. The check should include archived bookmarks too.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Warn-don't-block (allowing duplicates via 'Save anyway') contradicts REF-BM-06 (guide to editing the existing bookmark instead of creating a new one) and the duplicate-convergence edge rule. Client supplies the conforming prevent-and-redirect-to-edit behavior. Implemented round 14.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 maker: 'You can edit the Title, Description, Tags, and Note, but not the web address itself... Is that right, or do you want to edit the address too?' REF-BM-04 includes editing url. Round 14 client: 'I do need to edit the web address as well... Please include it in the editor, while still preventing it from being changed to another address that already exists.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Making url non-editable contradicts REF-BM-04 (edit url/title/description/tags/note). Client supplies the conforming behavior (editable address with collision guard). Implemented round 15.
